newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish construction firm plans IPO, bourse entry.
newsitem.headline: Polish construction firm plans IPO, bourse entry.

text.p: Polish construction company Unibud SA plans to issue between 700,000 and one million shares in its initial public offering and enter the parallel market of the Warsaw bourse, the firm's president said.
Jan Mikoluszko told Reuters on Wednesday the issue price was already set in the range of between 10 and 15 zlotys.
"We plan an initial public offering late in January or early in February," he said.
Currently the company, which is 51-percent owned by its employees and 49-percent by Budimex, has 660,000 shares.
Mikoluszko said the bourse debut was likely in the second quarter of 1997.
He said the company, based in Bielsk Podlaski, eastern Poland, had a net profit of 1.3 million zlotys on sales of 44 million zlotys in 1995.
It expects its 1996 net to rise to two million zlotys and its sales to 66 million zlotys.
